articles.title: Xbox at 25: My Memories From Across Xbox’s Entire (and Quite Incredible) History
articles.summary: I’ve been lucky enough to have a front-row seat for most of the Xbox’s 25 years, covering the high highs and low lows of Microsoft’s pivot into the living room. It’s been quite a ride since November 15, 2001, and I wanted to mark the occasion by sharing some of my biggest memories with you.
body: The first day of my career was October 1, 2002. I’d been lucky enough to get hired by Official Xbox Magazine. The fledgling Xbox console was not quite a year old, and when I got settled in on the staff, it quickly became clear that Xbox was really about one thing above all else: Halo. I remember being surprised in my first days on the job by what would happen every single day, like clockwork, at 5pm: consoles and TVs would get turned on, Halo would get fired up, and we’d all play a round or two of Capture the Flag on Blood Gulch before we all went home. Fun and friendly banter ensued. Halo was baked into the Xbox’s DNA from the very start.

But thanks to Combat Evolved carrying the Xbox through its first trip around the sun, things got really interesting in Year Two. It turns out I joined the magazine at just the right time! Halo: Combat Evolved was the biggest very real reason to buy the console in its first year, but its critical second year was defined by three things: Xbox Live, Tom Clancy games, and BioWare.
points: I’ve been lucky enough to have a front-row seat for most of the Xbox’s 25 years, covering the high highs and low lows of Microsoft’s pivot into the living room.

articles.title: 8 Must-Play Open-World RPGs for People With Real-Life Schedules
articles.summary: Raise your hand if this has ever happened to you: A friend texts you a screenshot of a map with 400 icons on it and the message “you’re going to love this game.” You’re excited — the map is detailed, the game looks great, and you do love it…for about 10 seconds.
body: If you’re looking for open-world RPGs you can actually play with a busy schedule, start here. These eight games range from true open-world adventures you can finish in a few weekends to RPG giants like Mass Effect that can be made manageable if you play them one mission at a time. Remember this: Keep it to just one quest tonight. The rest of the map will still be there when you get back.

Two kings walk into a war. One has whiskers. One has a wagging tail. Neither wants to be there. Cat Quest 2 is a 2D open-world action RPG set in a fantasy realm of cats and dogs where those kings are brought together against their will during a war between the cats of Felingard and the advancing dogs of the Lupus Empire, and both of them want their thrones back. The humor — as you might expect — leans on delightfully pun-heavy wordplay.

articles.title: Police arrest suspect after drive-by shooting at office campus housing Xbox studio inXile
articles.summary: Police have arrested a suspect after a drive-by shooting at an office campus in Tustin, California, which is home to Xbox-owned studio inXile Entertainment.
body: According to Aftermath, officers responded to reports of a drive-by shooting at Flight at Tustin Legacy, a campus that houses inXile and other businesses, on 11th November.

"Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt," Tustin Police Sergeant Christopher Peterson told the outlet. "Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."
"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," an inXile spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."
Police have not given a motive, and the suspect has not been named.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077 mod Torrent adds 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City
articles.summary: A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.
body: As spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

The rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.
The mod complements this with a new lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.
If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.
points: A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

articles.title: The 2026 GOTY Race Could Be a Disaster for Indie Games
articles.summary: Some quibble with the definition of Clair Obscur, a sizable production, as an indie game. (For what it's worth, the studio that made it is independent, and its publisher Kepler Interactive was founded by a collective of indie studios; it's definitely culturally indie.) But even if you excluded it…
body: Last year was a watershed moment for indie games at The Game Awards. Three games were nominated for both Game of the Year and Best Independent Game: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Hades 2, and Hollow Knight: Silksong. Together, they made up half of the GOTY 2025 field.

If you interpret this result as a sure sign that The Game Awards is taking indie games much more seriously, I'm afraid you might be disappointed. The 2025 nominations flatter to deceive, and 2026 looks like it will be a different matter. All three 2025 indie GOTY nominees were huge sellers, and two of them were high-profile sequels to critical darlings and popular favorites. These were not normal times. In previous years things were much more patchy. Balatro, 2024's indie nominee, was a massive viral hit. There was no indie nominee in 2023. In 2022, the lucky game was the distinctly slick and mainstream Stray. Prior to that, one indie game would typically break through every other year.
points: Some quibble with the definition of Clair Obscur, a sizable production, as an indie game.

articles.title: Super Meat Boy Is Officially Getting Remade Without Edmund McMillen's Involvement
articles.summary: Team Meat announced Super Meat Boy Again+, a remake of the classic indie platformer, during a Sweet 16 Birthday VIP Event on Nov. 14. While the announcement was meant to be celebratory, it has reminded people of the falling out that Super Meat Boy and Mewgenics creator Edmund McMillen has had with…
body: Team Meat describes Super Meat Boy Again+ on its Steam page as "everything you remember from Super Meat Boy presented through the wonderful lens of nostalgia with stuff added to it." In practice, that means it's a remake with art, music, cutscenes, and secrets for players to discover. Super Meat Boy Again+ does not currently have a release window.

We learned shortly after Super Meat Boy Again+'s reveal that Edmund McMillen wasn't involved in the project, despite being a co-creator of the franchise. On X, he posted the GIF of Homer Simpson backing up into bushes in response to a Wario64 post about the game's announcement. When another X user asked if he had anything to do with Super Meat Boy Again+, McMillen simply replied, "It's all news to me man."

Edmund McMillen co-founded Team Meat and designed the original Super Meat Boy, but he had left the studio by 2017. Since then, co-founder and programmer Tommy Refenes has continued to run Team Meat as CEO and has expanded the franchise since McMillen's departure with games like Super Meat Boy Forever, Dr. Fetus' Mean Meat Machine, and this year's Super Meat Boy 3D.

articles.title: Treyarch lays off lead Call of Duty writer and Zombies veteran after "approximately 20 years" of service
articles.summary: Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer. In a post made to both his Twitter/X account and LinkedIn, the developer thanked fans for their support during his two decades with the company and confirmed he was…
body: "After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts. "I am proud to have worked with so many talented people - many of whom will remain friends for life. Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years."

On Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message. It appears the layoffs referenced are part of the broad reorganistation affecting 3200 jobs that Xbox announced earlier this year. Treyarch, as part of Activision Blizzard, is owned by Xbox.

Houston is a bonafide veteran of the esteemed FPS series. His first Call of Duty title at Treyarch was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor. This was followed by World at War, Black Ops 1 through 4, where he is credited as a writer and designer. For Modern Warfare, Black Ops - Cold War, Vanguard, Modern Warfare 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7, he is listed as a member of the design team and in 'creative development'. He is not credited on this year's Modern Warfare 4.
points: Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer.

articles.title: Blade Runner 2099 bosses hint at a possible "triple-A" Blade Runner game in the future - just don't expect it any time soon
articles.summary: Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that.
body: In a new interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

Of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

articles.title: League of Legends will get an overhaul called New Dawn with new visuals, build options, and an updated client
articles.summary: Riot has announced a League of Legends overhaul that promises to touch every aspect of the game. "We want League to stand the test of time and be a game that's here for many years to come," said League Studio head Andrei "Meddler" van Roon in a teaser trailer.
body: The headlining changes coming with the update, called New Dawn, are a "modernized" client, a graphical revamp for the 5v5 map Summoner's Rift (the last time this happened was in 2014 ), and "new ways to play" each champion.

While details are scarce in the teaser, some brief footage is shown where you can see what he's talking about: a Blitzcrank player selects what looks like a character-specific mastery tree labeled "God Hand," and it cuts to him beating up an enemy in melee. Other champions are shown using abilities in ways they currently can't—Vayne, for instance, dashes through a wall.

An updated art style is also shown off, including new character models for all sorts of champions as well as bosses like Baron Nashor and the Elder Dragon. It looks much more in line with the art style of Wild Rift, League of Legends' mobile port-slash-spinoff with high-detail character models.
Player reactions are, as you might expect with an update that promises to be so comprehensive, all over the map.

articles.title: The pandemic was transformative for Jackbox: 'We went from a gamer name to a household name'
articles.summary: It's no secret that the Covid-19 pandemic saw a lot of people using videogames to stave off lockdown blues, and the Jackbox Party Pack games were especially well-suited for the role: easy-to-understand party fare that's optionally family-friendly and easy to play over a video call.
body: In a recent interview with PC Gamer associate editor Ted Litchfield, Jackbox Games CEO Mike Bilder said that the pandemic proved transformative for the developer.

"The industry at large obviously saw a lot of success at that time, but we did as well, and we went from a gamer name to a household name," he said, noting it was an "unfortunate period of time for the world, but for the gaming industry, a good one, and for Jackbox, a good one as well."

"That was kind of a leveling up for Jackbox as a company," said Bilder. "Suddenly office workers are doing happy hours and families over weekends are connecting over a game of Whiplash or something because it's what you did when you were locked down. People realized how easy it was to just share the screen over a Zoom call and everyone's playing."
It surprised employees at the studio to see how popular the games had become.

articles.title: GTA 6 Is Like The Olympics – “A Rare Cultural Moment” With Massive Ripple Effects
articles.summary: After years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19.
body: Francis Lawrence, the director of the new Hunger Games movie Sunrise on the Reaping, which comes out a day after GTA 6, has said he hopes people can find the time to play the game and watch his movie. In short, GTA 6 is seen by some as a black hole that will suck up time, attention, and money from the broader gaming economy--and even workplaces, as people dive into the 80-hour game they've been waiting a decade to play.

To help make sense of, and contextualize, the enormity of GTA 6's looming launch, GameSpot caught up with Bart Spiegel of the global professional services and research company PricewaterhouseCoopers, or PwC. He told GameSpot that GTA 6 is "something much bigger than a traditional entertainment launch," and is more akin to an event like the Olympics.
He believes GTA 6 is a "rare cultural moment" that "commands extraordinary attention and creates economic activity well beyond the event itself."

articles.title: YouTuber and comedian Ashens has 1,000 hours in Baldur's Gate 3 and reveals the worst retro game he's ever played: 'By the time you've hacked it to work, it's just no fun whatsoever'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Stuart Ashen—better known by his YouTube persona Ashens—grew up on a diet of 8-bit games on consoles like the Atari 2600 and the Spectrum. The earliest PC game he recalls playing was Syndicate Wars on his first home-built rig—a Pentium 200 MMX machine housed in a server tower case: "I loved Syndicate. Hated Syndicate Wars. Never got on with it at all," he says. "Ended up giving it to a friend who loved it … I think I went on to Duke Nukem 3D or something."

Alongside his video work, Ashens is currently making a folk horror film told in reverse. "Unfortunately, it's far enough away from release that there's no point plugging it," he says. But he hit pause on production to guide me through the haunted arcade of his PC. We talked DOS fighting games, the problem with rangers in RPGs, and the worst retro game Ashens has ever played.

articles.title: Slay the Spire 2 has a new character in testing, and she's really quite busted
articles.summary: Slay the Spire 2 has a new character—notably, a new character in testing —and as the patch notes themselves point out, that testing will very much be needed: "We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch." I decided to hop into the…
body: I decided to hop into the beta branch myself and take her for a whirl, and—yeah, those changes'll have to come. The Fool's central mechanic is her bow and arrow—she can fire an arrow/shoot card to deal damage equal to the card's base damage plus her aim. So if a shoot card deals 15 damage and she has six aim stocked, she'll deal 21.

This is a little busted, because by default, the Fool has 6 aim already put in her bank. Her non-strike starter card, Foolish Shot, already deals a hefty 15 damage for just one energy. With aim, the first time she uses it, it deals a whopping 21 damage, which is a heck of a damage output for the Fool's first round of combat.

The saving grace here is that when a card that fires an arrow is used, that arrow becomes lodged in a target, who gains the Impale status. You can't play any more arrow-based cards until you either Dislodge (another game term, hence the proper nounage) an arrow with a card that dislodges, or until you have more than one arrow.

articles.title: The Sunday Papers
articles.summary: While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here?
body: Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promised Mascot Agency.

A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

videos.title: DF Retro Super Show #027: The Legend of Zelda - Ocarina of Time - N64/3DS Revisited
videos.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has been remade for the Nintendo Switch 2 - and it's incredible. In this episode, the core-four reminisce about their experience with the Zelda series before the hugely important "Zelda 64" arrived in 1998.
points: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has been remade for the Nintendo Switch 2 - and it's incredible.
In this episode, the core-four reminisce about their experience with the Zelda series before the hugely important "Zelda 64" arrived in 1998.
From there, they get into their thoughts on the game and how it pushed video games forward.
Beyond that, they briefly touch on Nintendo 3DS remaster before finally tackling the 2026 remake.
videos.author: Digital Foundry

videos.title: Metro 2033/Last Light: PS5/Pro/Xbox Series X|S Upgrade Tested - Can All Consoles Run at 120Hz?
body: To stoke excitement for the impending Metro 2039, 4A Games revisits the first two games in the series with a 4K and 60FPS upgrade on PS5 and Xbox Series X. Texture quality is boosted, and ambient occlusion is improved - and there's even a 120Hz mode to further sweeten the deal (at a resolution hit). Tom runs through all the improvements compared to the last-gen release.
